defects.location_anchor: Section 2.1 Prelim (Sparse Autoencoder paragraph); after "Here, each activated element of $\rvc_t$ is interpreted as a concept."
defects.detection_criteria: HIT iff a finding flags the Section 2.1 assumption that the SAE reconstruction is lossless (equivalently: that extracted concepts fully preserve the hidden-state information) as unrealistic, unjustified, contradictory to TopK sparsity/the reconstruction-loss training, or never validated/discussed downstream. The finding must reference this lossless/information-preserving reconstruction assumption; generic doubts about SAE quality or concept interpretability that do not mention the assumption are a MISS.
defects.rationale: TopK SAEs are inherently lossy (the paragraph itself says the SAE is trained by minimizing a nonzero reconstruction loss), so asserting exact reconstruction is a strong idealization; it is stated once and never used, justified, or revisited anywhere downstream - the exact D8 pattern. Uses the paper's own macros, reading like a casual author idealization.
defects.old_string: Here, each activated element of $\rvc_t$ is interpreted as a concept.
defects.new_string: Here, each activated element of $\rvc_t$ is interpreted as a concept. Throughout this work, we assume the SAE reconstruction is lossless, i.e., $\widehat{\rvh}_t^{\mathtt{con}} = \rvh_t^{\mathtt{con}}$, so that the extracted concepts fully preserve the information encoded in the hidden state.

defects.location_anchor: Section 3 Experiments, \textbf{Evaluation setup.} paragraph; after "...even when the model was trained on a different corpus."
defects.detection_criteria: HIT iff a finding flags the Evaluation setup sentence stating that the reported checkpoint is the one attaining the highest average downstream-task accuracy, identifying it as test-set-based model selection, evaluation contamination/leakage, or an unfair/biased protocol (selecting on the very benchmarks being reported). The finding must target checkpoint/model selection based on downstream (evaluation) performance; generic requests for more evaluation details or seeds are a MISS.
defects.rationale: Selecting the reported checkpoint by the average accuracy on the seven reported evaluation benchmarks leaks the test metric into model selection - the taxonomy's train/test-overlap trap in a subtler form than "tuned on the test split". One innocuous-sounding sentence, mentioned nowhere else, in a plausible spot; deliberately worded around checkpoints (not hyperparameters) to stay independent of V2-4.
defects.old_string: We also consider OpenWebMath \citep{paster2023openwebmath} as a pretraining dataset to demonstrate that concepts learned from a pretrained LLM can still be applied to \sname, even when the model was trained on a different corpus.
defects.new_string: We also consider OpenWebMath \citep{paster2023openwebmath} as a pretraining dataset to demonstrate that concepts learned from a pretrained LLM can still be applied to \sname, even when the model was trained on a different corpus. For each method, we report the checkpoint that attains the highest average downstream-task accuracy.

defects.location_anchor: Section 3.3 Analysis of CoCoMix's effectiveness; paragraph headed "\textbf{Effectiveness of the attribution score.}"
defects.detection_criteria: HIT iff a finding points out inconsistent naming of the concept-selection score - i.e., that Section 3.3 uses "saliency score" while the method section (Sec. 2.2) and Figure 5(a)'s caption use "attribution score", or that "saliency score" is used without ever being defined/introduced. The finding must mention at least one of the two terms ("saliency score" or "attribution score"). Complaints about other naming issues (e.g., K_SAE vs K_concept, insertion vs mixing) are a MISS.
defects.rationale: Renames "attribution score" to "saliency score" consistently within one analysis paragraph (all 4 occurrences in one contiguous span), while Sec. 2.2's definition of a_t, the Figure 5(a) subcaption, and the main figure caption still say "attribution score" - the classic renamed-one-section-forgot-the-rest slip (the cited works are literally saliency-map papers, making the slip plausible). Verified "saliency" appears nowhere in the original.
defects.old_string: \textbf{Effectiveness of the attribution score.} We first analyze whether the attribution score effectively extracts important concepts. To demonstrate this, we train \sname using the activation value $\rvc_t$ for concept extraction, i.e., $\mathcal{L}_{\mathtt{concept}}(\rvc_t)$ in \autoref{eq:concept_pred}, instead of the attribution score $\rva_t$. Remark that the activation value also well reflects the importance of the concept \citep{bricken2023monosemanticity}. As shown in \autoref{fig:attribution_effect}, using attribution scores significantly improves performance
defects.new_string: \textbf{Effectiveness of the saliency score.} We first analyze whether the saliency score effectively extracts important concepts. To demonstrate this, we train \sname using the activation value $\rvc_t$ for concept extraction, i.e., $\mathcal{L}_{\mathtt{concept}}(\rvc_t)$ in \autoref{eq:concept_pred}, instead of the saliency score $\rva_t$. Remark that the activation value also well reflects the importance of the concept \citep{bricken2023monosemanticity}. As shown in \autoref{fig:attribution_effect}, using saliency scores significantly improves performance

defects.location_anchor: Appendix A Experimental Details, \textbf{Training details.} paragraph; between "...$\beta_1 = 0.9$ and $\beta_2 = 0.95$." and "For the KD baseline, we employed the vanilla KD loss..."
defects.detection_criteria: HIT iff a finding points out that the value of the concept-prediction loss coefficient lambda and/or the number of selected concepts K_attr is never reported (lambda is only called "a tunable coefficient" in Eq. 4 and K_attr is never given a value), harming reproducibility of CoCoMix training. The finding must name lambda, K_attr, the concept-loss weight, or the number of concepts selected per position. Complaints about other hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, K_SAE/SAE size, lambda_KD) are a MISS.
defects.rationale: Deletes the single sentence containing the only occurrence of the two method-specific hyperparameter values (lambda=0.1, K_attri=4); post-edit the main text still introduces both symbols with no value anywhere, and unlike the SAE settings they cannot be recovered from any citation. A one-sentence omission that looks exactly like an author oversight while making CoCoMix irreproducible.
defects.old_string: For training \sname, the concept prediction loss \autoref{eq:final} was scaled by a hyperparameter $\lambda = 0.1$, and $K_{\mathtt{attri}}$ was set to 4.

defects.location_anchor: Table 1 (tab:baseline) header, second row; after "\multirow{2}{*}{Method} & \multirow{2}{*}{\makecell{Total\\ Params}} & OWT & LAMB & Wiki ..."
defects.detection_criteria: HIT iff a finding points out that Table 1 (the NTP/KD/CoCoMix comparison table, tab:baseline) lacks metric-direction indicators - no up/down arrows or "higher/lower is better" marking for its PPL/Acc columns - or that the direction of improvement is not indicated in that table's header/caption. Direction-indicator complaints about figure subcaptions (which retain their arrows) or other table issues (bolding, rules) are a MISS.
defects.rationale: Strips all direction arrows from the only table's header row in one contiguous edit, directly instantiating the taxonomy's judge criterion (direction not marked). The caption-position sub-variant was unusable (caption already sits below the table in the original), and every figure subcaption retains its arrows, keeping the omission cleanly localized to Table 1. A different surface type from V1's D10/D11, as required.
